title: Practice exam 1
kicker: 50 new questions written from your lesson content. None of them are on your lesson tests. Answers are checked, not from an official key.

quiz.q: Complementary (solid) foods generally begin at around:
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Solids generally start around six months, when the baby shows readiness signs. (Lesson 10: Vegetarian Diets in Infancy)

quiz.q: Grains tend to be relatively lower in which amino acid?
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Grains tend to be relatively lower in lysine, while legumes tend to be relatively lower in methionine. Lower doesn’t mean absent. (Lesson 3: Protein and the nutritional value of beans)

quiz.q: Vitamin B12 is made by microorganisms, not by plants or animals.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. B12 is microbial in origin. Animals get it from bacteria; vegans need fortified foods or supplements. (Lesson 6: Vitamins)

quiz.q: What is a direct vegetarian source of DHA and EPA?
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Microalgae oil provides DHA (and sometimes EPA) directly. Sea vegetables aren’t a reliable substitute and can be very high in iodine. (Lesson 5: Fats)

quiz.q: A whole grain has had the bran and germ removed.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. A whole grain keeps all three parts. Refined grains keep mostly the endosperm. (Lesson 4: Carbohydrates)

quiz.q: Unplanned weight loss in an older adult is a warning sign that needs follow-up.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Energy needs may drop with age, but unplanned weight loss signals that intake isn’t meeting needs or that something else is going on. (Lesson 13: Vegetarian Diets for Older People)

quiz.q: Which features of many vegetarian diets can help lower LDL cholesterol?
o: More nuts, seeds and plant sterols
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. All three can help lower LDL. The effect depends on the actual foods: lots of cheese, butter or coconut fat can keep saturated fat high without any meat. (Lesson 2: Vegetarianism for Health)

quiz.q: Which pattern includes eggs but not dairy products?
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Ovo vegetarians eat eggs but not dairy. Lacto is dairy only, vegans avoid both, and lacto-ovo includes both. (Lesson 1: Vegetarianism)

quiz.q: Which vitamins are fat-soluble?
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Vitamins A, D, E and K are fat-soluble. The B vitamins and vitamin C are water-soluble. (Lesson 6: Vitamins)

quiz.q: Glycemic load is calculated as:
o: GI × grams of available carbohydrate in the serving ÷ 100
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Glycemic load = GI × available carbohydrate in the serving ÷ 100. Portion size changes the GL without changing the GI. (Lesson 4: Carbohydrates)

quiz.q: The amount of vitamin B12 in breast milk depends on the mother’s B12 status.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Milk B12 and iodine depend on the mother’s intake and status, while milk calcium is relatively protected. (Lesson 9: Vegetarian Diets — Pregnancy & Lactation)

quiz.q: All plant beverages, such as almond, rice and oat drinks, have about the same protein as cow’s milk.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Protein varies widely. Soy beverage is close to cow’s milk, but almond and rice drinks are much lower. (Lesson 8: Designing a Vegetarian Diet)

quiz.q: The iron found in plant foods is called:
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Plant foods provide nonheme iron, which is absorbed less well than the heme iron found in meat. (Lesson 7: Minerals)

quiz.q: Which first foods can help meet an infant’s rising iron needs?
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Iron-fortified cereal, legumes and tofu can all contribute iron. Serving a vitamin C food at the same time helps absorption. (Lesson 10: Vegetarian Diets in Infancy)

quiz.q: Folic acid only needs to start once a pregnancy is confirmed.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Neural tube development happens very early, often before a pregnancy is known, so folic acid starts before conception. (Lesson 9: Vegetarian Diets — Pregnancy & Lactation)

quiz.q: For someone with chronic kidney disease, potassium, phosphorus and protein targets depend mainly on:
o: The stage of kidney disease, lab results and treatment
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Kidney advice must match disease stage, labs and treatment such as dialysis. A vegetarian label is only the starting context. (Lesson 2: Vegetarianism for Health)

quiz.q: Responsive feeding means keeping a predictable meal and snack routine while respecting a child’s hunger and fullness signals.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Parents decide what and when; the child decides how much. Pressure and bribes tend to backfire. (Lesson 11: Vegetarian Diets for Children)

quiz.q: Calcium from spinach is well absorbed.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Spinach is high in oxalate, which binds calcium and lowers absorption. Low-oxalate greens such as kale and bok choy are absorbed well. (Lesson 7: Minerals)

quiz.q: Which nutrients does a vegan meal plan need to secure deliberately across the day?
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. A reusable vegan template secures B12, calcium and vitamin D, ALA and iodine every day. (Lesson 8: Designing a Vegetarian Diet)

quiz.q: Enriched white flour is the same as whole-grain flour.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Enrichment adds back some vitamins and iron, but not the fibre and other nutrients lost with the bran and germ. (Lesson 4: Carbohydrates)

quiz.q: Low energy availability in a teen athlete can happen even at a normal body size.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Normal body size doesn’t rule it out. Changes in periods, bone, growth or performance need assessment. (Lesson 12: Vegetarian Diets for Adolescents)

quiz.q: How many amino acids are considered indispensable (essential) for adults?
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Nine amino acids are indispensable for adults, because the body can’t make enough of them. (Lesson 3: Protein and the nutritional value of beans)

quiz.q: Most studies showing health benefits of vegetarian diets are observational, so they show associations rather than proof of cause.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Vegetarians often differ in smoking, activity and other habits. Observational studies can adjust for some of this, but they can’t prove the diet alone caused the outcome. (Lesson 2: Vegetarianism for Health)

quiz.q: Many prenatal supplements contain little or no choline.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Choline needs rise in pregnancy and lactation, but many prenatal supplements contain little or none, so food sources need review. (Lesson 9: Vegetarian Diets — Pregnancy & Lactation)

quiz.q: Most young children can meet their needs on a diet of fruits and vegetables alone.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Produce is bulky and low in energy. Children need energy- and nutrient-dense foods such as legumes, tofu, nut and seed butters and fortified products. (Lesson 11: Vegetarian Diets for Children)

quiz.q: Which helps a busy vegetarian teen eat consistently?
o: Portable snacks that pair carbohydrate with protein
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Mapping the school and sport day and packing portable carbohydrate-plus-protein snacks protects energy and growth. (Lesson 12: Vegetarian Diets for Adolescents)

quiz.q: Canned and frozen vegetables and beans can be useful, affordable choices for vegetarian meals.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Ordinary grocery aisles support the pattern well. Rinsing canned beans lowers sodium. (Lesson 14: Practical Applications of Vegetarianism)

quiz.q: Which is a more predictable source of iodine?
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Iodized salt is more predictable. Specialty salts may not be iodized, and seaweed iodine varies widely and can be excessive. (Lesson 7: Minerals)

quiz.q: A macrobiotic diet is always vegan.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Macrobiotic patterns vary. Many centre on whole grains, vegetables, beans and fermented soy, but some versions include fish or other animal foods. (Lesson 1: Vegetarianism)

quiz.q: During pregnancy, which nutrient does a vegan need from a reliable fortified food or supplement?
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. B12 has no reliable unfortified plant source, so a vegan pregnancy needs a planned B12 source. (Lesson 9: Vegetarian Diets — Pregnancy & Lactation)

quiz.q: Which is the essential omega-3 fatty acid?
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. ALA is the essential omega-3 fat. LA is the essential omega-6; oleic is an omega-9 the body can make. (Lesson 5: Fats)

quiz.q: An ordinary plant beverage, such as almond or oat drink, can replace infant formula.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Plant beverages are not infant formula. Breast milk or commercial infant formula is the main feed in the first year. (Lesson 10: Vegetarian Diets in Infancy)

quiz.q: A person taking warfarin must cut out all leafy greens.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. With warfarin, the key is keeping vitamin K intake consistent and monitored, not removing greens. (Lesson 13: Vegetarian Diets for Older People)

quiz.q: Vitamin D usually needs explicit planning for vegetarian teens, through fortified foods or a supplement.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Few foods provide much vitamin D naturally, and sun exposure varies, so it needs a planned source. (Lesson 12: Vegetarian Diets for Adolescents)

quiz.q: Plant proteins are missing some of the nine indispensable (essential) amino acids.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Plant foods contain all the indispensable amino acids. The proportions and digestibility differ from food to food. (Lesson 3: Protein and the nutritional value of beans)

quiz.q: The body converts ALA into DHA very efficiently.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Conversion of ALA to EPA is limited, and to DHA even more so. It also varies from person to person. (Lesson 5: Fats)

quiz.q: Seaweed and unfortified nutritional yeast are dependable sources of vitamin B12.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Neither is a reliable source of active B12. Vegans need B12-fortified foods or a supplement. (Lesson 1: Vegetarianism)

quiz.q: Which statement about plant beverages for children is accurate?
o: All plant beverages have the same protein as cow’s milk
Fortification varies by brand, so labels need checking
Rice beverage is the best protein choice
Plant beverages can replace infant formula
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Protein and fortification differ by product and country, so compare labels. Soy beverage is closest to cow’s milk in protein. (Lesson 11: Vegetarian Diets for Children)

quiz.q: Added calcium in fortified plant beverages stays evenly mixed, so there’s no need to shake the carton.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Added calcium can settle, so shaking the carton helps you get the amount on the label. (Lesson 8: Designing a Vegetarian Diet)

quiz.q: Which helps an older vegetarian maintain muscle?
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Protein distribution, resistance work and enough energy work together. Disease and frailty can change the plan. (Lesson 13: Vegetarian Diets for Older People)

quiz.q: Which foods are concentrated sources of ALA?
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Flax, chia, hemp, walnuts and canola or soy oil all supply ALA. (Lesson 5: Fats)

quiz.q: When replacing an egg in a recipe, the first step is to:
o: Work out what job the egg does, such as binding, leavening or moisture
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Different replacers suit different jobs: flax or chia and tofu bind, aquafaba foams, banana adds moisture to sweet baking. (Lesson 14: Practical Applications of Vegetarianism)

quiz.q: Honey is a safe sweetener for babies from six months of age.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Honey can carry spores that cause infant botulism, so it’s avoided in the first year. (Lesson 10: Vegetarian Diets in Infancy)

quiz.q: Which is the best first step when assessing someone who says they are vegetarian?
o: Tell them which type of vegetarian they really are
Ask what foods, fortified products and supplements they actually use
Assume their diet is low in protein
Assume their diet is healthier than average
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. The label is only a starting point. Two people with the same label can eat very differently, so assessment starts with the actual foods, fortified products and supplements. (Lesson 1: Vegetarianism)

quiz.q: Which blood test is usually used to check vitamin D status?
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. 25-hydroxyvitamin D is the usual status marker. Ferritin reflects iron stores; methylmalonic acid helps clarify B12 status. (Lesson 6: Vitamins)

quiz.q: A high folate intake can hide the anemia of B12 deficiency while nerve damage continues.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Folate can correct the blood signs of B12 deficiency, but it can’t prevent the neurologic damage. (Lesson 6: Vitamins)

quiz.q: When total energy intake is too low, the body is more likely to use protein for fuel.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Energy and protein are linked. With too few calories, amino acids are burned for energy and body tissue may be broken down. (Lesson 3: Protein and the nutritional value of beans)

quiz.q: A diet based on refined grains, sweets and large amounts of cheese can be vegetarian.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Vegetarian only describes what is left out. Diet quality depends on what replaces the meat. (Lesson 2: Vegetarianism for Health)

quiz.q: Vegetarians need to combine complementary proteins at the same meal.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Healthy adults get a full range of amino acids from varied foods eaten over the day. Same-meal combining isn’t needed. (Lesson 8: Designing a Vegetarian Diet)

quiz.q: Which practices can reduce phytate and improve mineral absorption?
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Soaking, sprouting (which activates phytase), fermenting and leavening bread can all improve access to minerals like iron and zinc. (Lesson 7: Minerals)

title: Practice exam 2
kicker: 50 new questions written from your lesson content. None of them are on your lesson tests. Answers are checked, not from an official key.

quiz.q: Vitamin B12 is water-soluble but can be stored in the body for a long time.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. B12 is water-soluble, yet the liver stores a lot of it, so deficiency can take years to show. (Lesson 6: Vitamins)

quiz.q: Rapid weight loss can raise the risk of gallstones, even on a healthy-sounding diet.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. NIDDK lists rapid weight loss as a gallstone risk, and recommends fibre-rich foods and healthy fats. (Lesson 2: Vegetarianism for Health)

quiz.q: People choose vegetarian diets for reasons such as:
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Motivations often overlap: ethics, environment, faith, family tradition, cost and health can all play a part. (Lesson 1: Vegetarianism)

quiz.q: Dried fruit is a more concentrated source of sugar and energy than the same fruit fresh.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Drying removes water, which concentrates sugar and energy. (Lesson 8: Designing a Vegetarian Diet)

quiz.q: Which helps meet a young child’s energy needs when stomachs are small?
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Energy- and nutrient-dense foods help small stomachs. Use safe textures to prevent choking. (Lesson 11: Vegetarian Diets for Children)

quiz.q: Vitamin C reduces the absorption of iron from plant foods.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Vitamin C enhances nonheme iron absorption. (Lesson 7: Minerals)

quiz.q: Blue and purple foods such as blueberries often contain:
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Anthocyanins give blue and purple colours. Lycopene is red and beta-carotene is orange. (Lesson 4: Carbohydrates)

quiz.q: Which iodine unit is used for pregnancy recommendations?
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Iodine recommendations are in micrograms. Mixing up mg and mcg is a 1,000-fold error. (Lesson 9: Vegetarian Diets — Pregnancy & Lactation)

quiz.q: Besides protein, a serving of beans provides:
o: Minerals such as iron and potassium
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Beans are a nutrient package: protein, starch, fibre, folate and several minerals together. (Lesson 3: Protein and the nutritional value of beans)

quiz.q: Beta-carotene is best described as:
o: A provitamin A carotenoid the body can convert to vitamin A
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Beta-carotene is a provitamin A carotenoid. Conversion is lower and more variable than getting preformed retinol. (Lesson 6: Vitamins)

quiz.q: Which can change what an older adult is able to eat?
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Oral health, dexterity, cognition and isolation all affect intake. Texture can be adapted without losing nutrients. (Lesson 13: Vegetarian Diets for Older People)

quiz.q: A simple vegetarian meal formula includes:
o: An energy base such as grains
Vegetables or fruit plus a fat or flavour
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Anchor each meal with protein, add an energy base, then produce and a fat or flavour. (Lesson 8: Designing a Vegetarian Diet)

quiz.q: Too much iodine can be as harmful as too little.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Iodine supports thyroid hormone, but excess, such as from heavy seaweed use, can cause thyroid problems. (Lesson 7: Minerals)

quiz.q: Canadian guidance waits until about age two before a fortified plant beverage becomes the main milk source.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Canada advises against fortified plant beverages as the main milk before age two; even then, choose a fortified soy beverage. (Lesson 10: Vegetarian Diets in Infancy)

quiz.q: DHA is concentrated in the retina and nervous tissue.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. DHA is a structural fat in the eye and brain. (Lesson 5: Fats)

quiz.q: Isoflavones in soy are the same as human estrogen.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Isoflavones are plant compounds that act much more weakly and selectively than human estrogen. (Lesson 12: Vegetarian Diets for Adolescents)

quiz.q: Antioxidant supplements give the same benefits as eating fruits and vegetables.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Supplements aren’t interchangeable with whole foods and can be harmful in some situations. (Lesson 2: Vegetarianism for Health)

quiz.q: Nutritional yeast is always fortified with vitamin B12.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Only some brands are fortified. Check the label. (Lesson 8: Designing a Vegetarian Diet)

quiz.q: Vegans avoid all animal-derived foods, including dairy and eggs.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. As a dietary practice, vegans avoid animal-derived foods; many also avoid honey. (Lesson 1: Vegetarianism)

quiz.q: Very high doses of preformed vitamin A can build up and become toxic, especially in pregnancy.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Preformed vitamin A accumulates. Pregnancy makes reviewing the dose especially important. (Lesson 6: Vitamins)

quiz.q: Cooking legumes has no effect on their lectins and enzyme inhibitors.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Proper heat makes legumes safe and more digestible. (Lesson 3: Protein and the nutritional value of beans)

quiz.q: Dietary fats spoil (oxidize) faster when exposed to:
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Oxygen, light, heat and time all promote oxidation. Flax oil and nuts keep best sealed, cool and dark. (Lesson 5: Fats)

quiz.q: Older adults may absorb less vitamin B12 from food, whatever diet they follow.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Age can impair absorption of food-bound B12, which is why fortified foods or supplements help. (Lesson 13: Vegetarian Diets for Older People)

quiz.q: Lentils need to soak overnight before cooking.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Small lentils cook quickly without soaking; bigger beans need longer. (Lesson 14: Practical Applications of Vegetarianism)

quiz.q: Puberty is a major period for building bone.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. A large share of adult bone is laid down in adolescence, so calcium, vitamin D, energy and activity matter. (Lesson 12: Vegetarian Diets for Adolescents)

quiz.q: Glycemic index tells you how much a usual serving of a food raises blood glucose.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. GI standardizes the carbohydrate amount. Glycemic load is the measure that accounts for the serving. (Lesson 4: Carbohydrates)

quiz.q: Vegetarian foods can carry foodborne pathogens, so food safety still matters in pregnancy.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Unpasteurized products, sprouts and poorly handled foods can carry pathogens. Safe handling matters for every pattern. (Lesson 9: Vegetarian Diets — Pregnancy & Lactation)

quiz.q: Raw-food and fruitarian diets are more restrictive than a varied vegan diet.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. They add limits on food groups or cooking, which raises the risk of low energy, protein, B12, calcium, iron and zinc. (Lesson 1: Vegetarianism)

quiz.q: Thiamin (vitamin B1) mainly supports:
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Thiamin supports energy metabolism. Variety in whole grains, legumes and seeds helps cover it. (Lesson 6: Vitamins)

quiz.q: Plant-based meat alternatives all have similar sodium, protein and saturated fat.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. They vary widely. Read the label to see how a product fits the overall diet. (Lesson 2: Vegetarianism for Health)

quiz.q: Brazil nuts provide a precise, predictable dose of selenium.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Selenium in plant foods varies with the soil, and Brazil nuts vary too much for exact dosing. (Lesson 7: Minerals)

quiz.q: When salt is used at home for a vegan child, it should be iodized salt.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Iodized salt is a measured iodine source. Seaweed iodine varies and can be excessive. (Lesson 11: Vegetarian Diets for Children)

quiz.q: A single growth measurement is enough to judge whether a child is growing well.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Serial measurements show the trajectory. One reading can mislead. (Lesson 11: Vegetarian Diets for Children)

quiz.q: Ground flax or chia mixed with water mainly replaces which egg function?
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. The gel from flax or chia binds ingredients together. It doesn’t whip into a foam the way aquafaba does. (Lesson 14: Practical Applications of Vegetarianism)

quiz.q: Bile helps fat digestion by:
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Bile emulsifies fat so lipase can digest it. Micelles then carry the products to intestinal cells. (Lesson 5: Fats)

quiz.q: Thirst may be a less reliable signal of fluid needs in older adults.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Older adults may feel less thirsty, so regular drinks and water-rich foods help. (Lesson 13: Vegetarian Diets for Older People)

quiz.q: Absorption of food B12 depends on:
o: Intrinsic factor and a healthy ileum
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. B12 binds intrinsic factor and is absorbed in the ileum. (Lesson 6: Vitamins)

quiz.q: Infant vitamin B12 deficiency can cause serious neurologic harm.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Infant B12 deficiency can damage development. Both the mother’s and the infant’s B12 plans need checking. (Lesson 10: Vegetarian Diets in Infancy)

quiz.q: Sweetened vanilla plant beverage is the best choice for savoury sauces and soups.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Choose flavour and sweetness to suit the recipe; unsweetened is the safer choice for sauces and soups. (Lesson 14: Practical Applications of Vegetarianism)

quiz.q: Zinc supports:
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Zinc supports enzymes, growth, repair, immunity and taste. (Lesson 7: Minerals)

quiz.q: When increasing fibre, it’s best to increase it gradually and drink enough fluid.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Going gradually and adding fluid improves tolerance. (Lesson 4: Carbohydrates)

quiz.q: In lactation, which nutrients in breast milk depend most on the mother’s intake?
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Milk B12 and iodine track the mother’s status. Milk calcium is relatively protected. (Lesson 9: Vegetarian Diets — Pregnancy & Lactation)

quiz.q: First-in, first-out rotation means using older pantry stock before newer stock.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Rotating stock keeps dry staples fresh and reduces waste. (Lesson 14: Practical Applications of Vegetarianism)

quiz.q: Legumes tend to be relatively lower in which amino acid?
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Legumes tend to be relatively lower in methionine; grains tend to be lower in lysine. Variety across the day covers both. (Lesson 3: Protein and the nutritional value of beans)

quiz.q: Delaying common allergens such as peanut is routinely recommended for infants.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Routine delay is outdated. Most infants can have allergens in a safe texture; high-risk infants need individual guidance. (Lesson 10: Vegetarian Diets in Infancy)

quiz.q: Older adults may benefit from about 1.0 g of protein per kg of body weight a day, plus resistance exercise.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. At least about 1.0 g/kg/day with resistance exercise may benefit older adults, though conditions can change the plan. (Lesson 3: Protein and the nutritional value of beans)

quiz.q: Which wording is most accurate for findings from observational vegetarian studies?
o: Vegetarian diets are associated with lower risk of some diseases
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Observational evidence supports "associated with". Cure or guarantee language overstates what these studies can show. (Lesson 2: Vegetarianism for Health)

quiz.q: Which is the essential omega-6 fatty acid?
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Linoleic acid (LA) is the essential omega-6. ALA is the essential omega-3. (Lesson 5: Fats)

quiz.q: Soaking, sprouting and leavened breads can help teens get more zinc from plant foods.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. These methods lower phytate, which otherwise reduces zinc absorption. (Lesson 12: Vegetarian Diets for Adolescents)

quiz.q: The tolerable upper intake level (UL) is a goal to aim for.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. The UL is a safety ceiling, not a target. (Lesson 9: Vegetarian Diets — Pregnancy & Lactation)
